coverageNotes.shelter: WMO global climate and ILO occupational heat; territorial CO2 excluding LULUCF, common year 2024.
coverageNotes.hold: Global care gap and labour-force exclusion; national sex pairs retain the survey year. Taiwan has a different age range and includes volunteering.
coverageNotes.space: UN-Habitat broad housing-inadequacy upper estimate (2026 report), cumulative informal-settlement eviction estimate (2003–2023), and 2024 urban slum indicators are different overlapping concepts. Taiwan model affordability is a separate national indicator.
coverageNotes.thirst: WHO/UNICEF JMP service levels. Safety not assured is not synonymous with confirmed contamination. Emergency 15 L is a WHO guideline, not population data.
coverageNotes.offline: ITU 2026 global estimates and distinct inequality dimensions; WDI national Internet-use comparison held at 2024.
coverageNotes.vacant: No harmonized global vacant-dwelling total is claimed. World cards provide housing-deprivation context, measured in people, not vacancy. National/city/administrative vacant-home definitions differ and are never summed or directly converted into people rehoused.

thirst.nonSafelyManagedMeaning: Safety/service standard not assured; do not label all of this water contaminated.

cards.definition: Up to 3.4 billion people worldwide lack secure, safe and adequate housing, as summarized in the 2026 report introduction and key findings. cards.definition: Estimated cumulative number of people displaced from informal settlements for urban development between 2003 and 2023. The report frames this as at least 64 million. Box 4.3 combines satellite imagery and local enumerations in 94 cities in Africa, Asia and Latin America (14% of the urban population in less developed regions) and extrapolates a weighted/averaged estimate. Monitoring is incomplete; not all forms of global eviction, not annual evictions and not a current displacement stock.
cards.nonAdditivity: Cumulative displacement over 2003–2023 is a different measure from current housing inadequacy or slum resident counts; populations can overlap and must not be summed.
